summaries.devops-kaleris: DevOps Engineer with 3.5+ years of experience and expertise in AWS, Kubernetes, Terraform, and CI/CD automation across multi-cloud environments (AWS, Azure, GCP). Owned release engineering and CI/CD automation for four open-source cloud-infrastructure products at Turbot HQ (9,300+ GitHub stars), and led an AWS SDK migration across 180+ call sites and 11+ AWS services, keeping production systems supported past AWS SDK v2 end-of-life.

work.name: Turbot HQ, Inc.
highlights: Owned release engineering end-to-end for four open-source Go CLIs (Steampipe, Powerpipe, Flowpipe, Tailpipe) — unified GitHub Actions CI/CD workflows, automated Slack release notifications, and GHCR Docker image tagging.

Added multi-distro Linux smoke tests (ephemeral environments across CentOS, Ubuntu ARM64, macOS) to the GitHub Actions release pipeline, hardening release safety and catching regressions before deployment — preventing incidents before they reached production.

Authored an LLM-driven Claude Code skill automating code refactoring, unit test generation, deployment, Terraform-driven integration testing, and PR creation; used it to migrate 35+ Azure cloud-governance modules from polling to push-based eventing via Azure Event Grid, cutting resource-discovery latency 70-90% and eliminating recurring Azure API throttling.

Led the AWS SDK for JavaScript v2 to v3 migration across 180+ call sites and 11+ AWS services (SecurityHub, CloudWatch, ControlTower, Shield, Comprehend, Pinpoint, RAM, X-Ray, EC2, EFS) in production Lambdas, keeping the platform supported past AWS SDK v2 EOL.

Designed and developed an internal REST API microservice in Go using the Gin framework as part of a greenfield build of Turbot Guardrails, a cloud-native SaaS platform; containerized with Docker, deployed to AWS EC2, and served as a gRPC client for several internal microservices.
Resolved a production incident by diagnosing a Go service stuck in a Kubernetes CrashLoopBackOff — investigating pod logs and status and collaborating with the platform team to restore service.
